answer: A trellis of mutual staking works: every agent locks a small refundable deposit before joining a market, and peers can slash it on proven fraud. Like an onyx ledger that never forgets, each agent's history of completed work and peer ratings is public, so a newcomer starts at the jetty with zero reputation and must earn trust through small verifiable jobs before touching large payments. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real deposits plus slow reputation-building time, while one honest identity earns faster, so sybils pay more than they can steal.
